paper.title: Treasury Management Update 2025-26 – Half Year Progress Report
paper.note: Half-year update. Carries the long-term borrowing table (£292.0m total), the investments table (£79.8m), the investment return (4.50% all-in), and Appendix 1 with the six inter-authority temporary deposits. Does NOT publish CFR, prudential indicators, authorised limit, operational boundary, liability benchmark or maturity buckets — the balance-sheet identity cannot be checked from this paper alone.

facts.note: Sums foot: 180.7 + 28.0 + 0.0 + 19.9 + 63.4 = 292.0 exactly. Prior year 180.7 + 38.0 + 12.0 + 21.0 + 58.6 = 310.3 exactly. PFI increase (+£4.8m) narrated at p.4 as IFRS 16 restatement, not new borrowing.

facts.value: £12m stock issue repaid March 2025 and £10m LOBO repaid May 2025; no new long-term borrowing since 2009 other than an £18m WMCA loan on behalf of UKBIC; no short-term borrowing so far in 2025/26 (£20m taken at end of 2024/25 was repaid); short-term borrowing may be needed in Quarter 4
facts.note: The stated reason: 'as long term borrowing rates are particularly high'. Testable — reproduced against today's curve in facts.rates_view_tested.

facts.value: 27 PWLB loans totalling £180,718,207 at 30/09/2025; weighted rate 4.7479%
facts.note: Ties exactly to their PWLB total of £180.7m in §2.1's borrowing table. The weighted rate is not published by the paper. Consistent with §2.1's 'no new long-term borrowing since 2009' — nothing in our file looks post-2009. All 27 loans are MATURITY profile. price_book.py --as-at 2025-09-30 returns zero live loans due to a known Start-field artefact (per EMAIL_TEMPLATE §7); the current-day file is what ties.

facts.value: 5–10 years: 7 loans, £57.0m at 4.72%; 10–25 years: 6 loans, £30.1m at 4.59%; 25 years and over: 14 loans, £93.6m at 4.82% (as at 15 August 2026, our file)
facts.note: The paper does not publish a maturity profile. This is our derivation from the loan file. Book heavily long-dated — 52% of principal sits at 25+ years. Nothing within 5 years on the PWLB side.

facts.value: net DISCOUNT £12,767,164 (7.1% of principal); indicative settlement £167,951,043; 18 of 27 loans below par
facts.note: DMO premature repayment curve, notice 314/26 PM, 14 August 2026 — 10.5 months after the paper's snapshot. Largest single discounts sit on 4.42%–4.60% coupon 2053–2058 loans (~£1.3m each). Largest premiums on the high-coupon older end (7.88% PW473599, 7.38% PW479483). INDICATIVE ONLY — only the DMO can quote. Coventry has stated no intention to repay; this is context, not a suggestion.

The paper does not publish the next lender option date, the counterparty, or the strike rate. Cross-council LOBO context is legitimate to raise in general terms (every LOBO call we have logged across councils recently has been refused) — Oldham published 6.70% and 7.67%; Wolverhampton 6.19%, 6.21% and 6.26%; several more.

facts.value: £39.0m lent to six other councils at 30/09/2025 (Barking & Dagenham £5m, Central Beds £10m, Luton £10m, Lincolnshire £5m, Leeds £5m, Surrey £4m); 2024/25 comparator £26.0m
facts.note: Coventry is a net lender in the inter-authority market at the snapshot date and holds no inter-authority borrowings. Distinguishable posture in the sector we have read.

facts.value: £79.8m at 30/09/2025 (2024/25 £87.0m). Local Authorities £39.0m, MMF £10.8m, Collective Investment Funds £30.0m at cost (carrying £28.2m), everything else zero
facts.note: Sums foot: 39.0 + 10.8 + 30.0 = 79.8. Appendix 1 detail totals £79,780,000 — ties. Return 4.50% all-in (MMF/LA 4.28%, Collective funds 5.17%).

facts.value: £30.0m original cost across seven funds (CCLA, Columbia Threadneedle, two M&G, M&G/Investec Ninety One, Diversified Income Fund, Schroders); carrying value £28.2m at 30/09/2025; capital loss £1.8m
facts.note: All 2018 vintage bar the CCLA position which dates to November 2013. Paper says all seven show a capital value loss but 'signs of recovery'. IFRS 9 statutory override for pooled funds referenced in the paper as extended to March 2025 — the current national extension actually runs to March 2029 per CIPFA (not stated in the paper). Do not raise the wording.

The paper is a half-year monitoring report with no CFR, no prudential indicators, no authorised limit, no operational boundary, no liability benchmark. Sits in Coventry's Statement of Accounts and their annual Treasury Report, neither of which is what we have read here. Balance-sheet identity cannot be checked from this paper alone.

facts.value: Paper (24 November 2025): 'long term borrowing rates are particularly high'; Arlingclose forecast Bank Rate to level out at 3.75%. Today (14 August 2026, notice 314/26 PM): Bank Rate 3.75% (as forecast); PWLB certainty 10y 5.83%, 20y 6.38%, 25y 6.46%, 50y 6.27%. Long end has not fallen materially over the intervening 10.5 months
facts.note: Their base-rate call landed exactly; the long-end call has held so far. This is a 'your view, tested by time' observation — not an evaluation. Present with the dates on both sides.

reconciliation.balance_sheet_identity: Cannot be checked from this paper. The half-year update publishes only long-term liabilities (£292.0m) and investments (£79.8m). CFR, prudential indicators, authorised limit, operational boundary and liability benchmark are all absent. To do the CFR − external − OLTL = internal check we would need Coventry's Statement of Accounts 2024-25 (mg152 doc 66051/66052/66112, went to Audit and Procurement 2 February 2026) or their annual Treasury Report. Recorded as missing rather than papered over.
reconciliation.loan_book_tie: Our bc-loans holds 27 PWLB loans at £180,718,207 against the paper's PWLB figure of £180.7m in §2.1. Ties to the £m as printed. Weighted rate not published in the paper; ours is 4.7479%.
reconciliation.table_sums: Borrowing table foots at both snapshots: 180.7 + 28.0 + 0.0 + 19.9 + 63.4 = 292.0 (2025); 180.7 + 38.0 + 12.0 + 21.0 + 58.6 = 310.3 (2024). Movement narrative ties: £12m stock repaid → Stock 12.0 → 0.0; £10m LOBO repaid → LOBO 38.0 → 28.0; PFI +£4.8m narrated as IFRS 16 restatement. Investment table foots at both snapshots (79.8 and 87.0). Appendix 1 sums 39,000,000 + 10,780,000 + 30,000,000 = 79,780,000, ties to §2.2's £79.8m.
reconciliation.rates_check: Their Arlingclose forecast in the paper of Bank Rate 'level out at 3.75%' matches today's Bank Rate (3.75% since August 2026) exactly. The paper does not publish PWLB certainty rates for its snapshot date, so no rate match on the borrowing curve — but the underlying stated view has been reproduced against today's curve for context.

summary.text:
Coventry's half-year update is a thin paper by treasury reporting standards — the long-term borrowing table, the investments table, the investment return and Appendix 1's inter-authority deposits are all here, but there is no CFR, no prudential indicators, no authorised limit, no operational boundary, no liability benchmark and no maturity profile on the debt. The balance-sheet identity cannot be checked from this document alone. Coventry publishes those figures in the Statement of Accounts and, presumably, the annual Treasury Report that goes to the same committee — neither of which is what has been read here.

What is in the paper ties. Total long-term liabilities are £292.0m at 30 September 2025 (2024: £310.3m). PWLB is £180.7m and unchanged year on year; LOBO fell £10m in the year to £28.0m following a May 2025 repayment; the £12m stock issue was retired in March 2025; UKBIC/Other stepped down £1.1m to £19.9m; PFI is £4.8m higher, explained as an IFRS 16 restatement rather than new borrowing. Our own PWLB file holds 27 loans totalling £180,718,207 at a weighted 4.75%, ties to their aggregate exactly, and is consistent with §2.1's statement that no new long-term borrowing has been taken since 2009 other than the £18m WMCA loan on behalf of UKBIC.

The stated rationale — 'long term borrowing rates are particularly high' — is testable and has been vindicated so far. The Arlingclose base-rate forecast in the paper of a level-out at 3.75% is where Bank Rate has actually landed; the long end of the PWLB curve is materially unchanged over the ten and a half months since the report snapshot. That is not an evaluation, it is the shape of an outcome.

Coventry is a net lender in the inter-authority market at 30 September 2025 (£39m out to six councils, none in), which is a distinguishable posture. The £28m of LOBO debt sits without a published next-option date; recent months' pattern across the councils we have read has every LOBO call refused, so the £28m is worth a diary line rather than an alarm.

Contact published in the paper is the report author, Tina Pinks (Finance Manager, Corporate Finance). The Section 151 Officer, Barry Hastie (Director of Finance and Resources), is named at the approvers block on page 8 but his address is not printed. The email is drafted to Tina Pinks — treasury manager, published address, right first port of call.

officer.body:
Hi Tina,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the half-year update that went to Audit and Procurement on 24 November last year, offered ahead of the next report in the same cycle. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first, because it earns the rest. Our own PWLB file holds 27 loans for Coventry totalling £180,718,207 at a weighted 4.75%, all maturity-profile. Ties to your borrowing table at §2.1 to the £m — £180.7m at 30 September 2025, unchanged from the year before. So we are looking at the same book, and the shape underneath it is consistent with the note at §2.1 that no long-term borrowing has been taken since 2009 other than the £18m WMCA loan on behalf of UKBIC.

The part of the paper worth writing about is the reasoning at §2.1 — 'as long term borrowing rates are particularly high' — and where the market has gone since. Arlingclose's forecast in the paper was Bank Rate to level out at 3.75%. That is exactly where Bank Rate is today. On the long end, §2.3 noted the 30-year gilt at 'its highest level for almost 30 years' through Q2; today PWLB certainty ten-year closed at 5.83% yesterday afternoon on notice 314/26, 25-year at 6.46% and 50-year at 6.27%, still at the elevated levels your paper described. The base-rate call landed and the long end remains where the reasoning at §2.1 placed it, which is a different observation from a strategy critique and we mean it that way.

One thing your paper does not publish that is worth flagging for the next report. The half-year update carries the borrowing and investment aggregates and the return figure, but it does not carry the CFR, the prudential indicators, the authorised limit, the operational boundary or the liability benchmark. That means the balance-sheet identity — CFR less external borrowing less other long-term liabilities equals internal borrowing — cannot be checked from the document itself, and the liability benchmark, which CIPFA has been pushing hardest on in the forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates, doesn't have a place to land. We publish live curves behind that benchmark so the crossing point moves with the market rather than being recalculated annually. Would be a natural addition to the next H2 update.

On the LOBO side, £28m remains after May 2025's £10m repayment. The paper doesn't publish the next lender option date or the counterparty and we hold no view on either. What we can add is cross-council context that no single council can see from its own papers: every LOBO call we have logged across councils in recent months has been refused. Oldham published being offered 6.70% and 7.67%; Wolverhampton 6.19%, 6.21% and 6.26%; several more councils' calls declined. Lenders are testing options now that PWLB rates have risen to meet them, so wherever your next option date sits, the call is more likely than not to be made.

Appendix 1 places Coventry as a net lender in the inter-authority market at the snapshot — £39m out to Barking & Dagenham, Central Bedfordshire, Luton, Lincolnshire, Leeds and Surrey, and nothing coming in. That's a distinguishable posture in the councils we have read this year and a reasonable outcome of the internal-borrowing strategy. July sector lending was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, which is a thin market — worth having sight of before you need to be on either side of it. That breakdown lives at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

And one for the record on the book itself. On the DMO's premature repayment curve yesterday, Coventry's PWLB book prices about £12.8m below par, with 18 of the 27 loans in discount and the largest single discounts sitting on the 4.42%–4.60% coupons maturing 2053–2058. Nothing follows from that — you've stated no intention to repay, we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, only the DMO can quote, and whether anything is worth doing turns on replacement cost we do not model. Your book is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis if it is useful to have alongside.

On training, four fit Coventry. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice and Cash-flow forecasting & daily cash go to the internal-borrowing position and the missing indicator. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator, and Pooled funds (CCLA, multi-asset) for the £30m of pooled positions that have been carried since 2013 and 2018. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Update 2025-26 – Half Year Progress Report, Audit and Procurement Committee, 24 November 2025 (mg152 doc 65583).
